task_contract.goal: the maximum of c1 over all words of a given length, and how many attain it
task_contract.counted: words of the given length over the label alphabet
task_contract.state: the twelve coordinates: the doubled centre and the frame. Nothing else is consulted, because legality is vacuous here
task_contract.notes: every word of the length is legal

grammar.note: the enumeration and its order are the grammar's; nothing is injected or excluded here

axis1.tie_break:
within one Pareto front, and only there: acquisition cost plus the cost of running the WORKLOAD THE TASK DECLARES -- its own answer lengths -- both counted in primitive calls, then the earlier candidate in the grammar's fixed enumeration order. Stated here rather than decided per run.
Why this and not the cheaper acquisition: a probe at a small length measures the wrong thing. An acquisition is paid once and the saving grows with the length actually asked for, so a tie-break on acquisition alone would hand every task to the route that learns nothing, whatever the task goes on to ask. Both sides of the ledger are measured over the same declared workload instead.
This does not reintroduce a weighting across the Pareto components: it is one quantity in one unit, used only to order candidates that the frontier has already declared incomparable.

premise.centre: symbolic; every integer centre is covered
premise.scope: exact for every frame the alphabet reaches within 4 folds and every centre

acquisition_cost.includes: the premise, and the closure and certification of EVERY candidate, refused ones included. A search pays for what it rejects.
acquisition_cost.excludes: the probe measurements below, which are comparison work and are reported separately

axis1.span_class_note: candidates spanning the same linear space are one representation, decided by exact rank on shared monomial coordinates. Only one member of each class is measured.

c1.primitive_count_note: zero here means the primitives this route uses are not instrumented, not that it did no work; read workload_nodes

tie_break_workload.units_disagree_note: the two units put a different candidate first. The stated rule uses wall time; the node order is kept here so the disagreement is visible rather than settled silently
